title: Point an AI assistant at data.un.org
idea: Connect it, ask, and watch it fetch rather than recall.
summary: Never ask a chatbot what a statistic is. Connect it to the UN System Data Commons MCP server and let it fetch the figure, with its unit and publisher.

transcript.text: Ask a chatbot for a UN statistic and it will give you a confident, plausible, invented number.
Pasting the table fixes that. Better still, let it fetch the figure itself — which is what the Commons publishes an M C P server for.
The address is on the Connect page under Build. No key, no account, no registration.
In Claude Code it is one command. In any other M C P client it is three lines of config. You do this once.
Then you just ask. It searches the corpus and comes back with candidate indicators and their identifiers — including, here, that two agencies measure this.
Then it fetches the observation. One hundred and fifteen point one one, for twenty twenty-three — and the unit and publisher come back attached to it.
That is the same number you found by hand in the first video. Nothing was remembered, nothing was guessed, and the citation arrived with the figure.
Check it anyway. Match a few figures against the tool output, and confirm the unit survived into your prose.
Connect it once, then ask what the numbers mean rather than what they are. That is the whole of using AI safely with official statistics.

tryIt.note: One line, once. It is named un-data so it does not clash with the undata package's connector. Any MCP client works; this is the shortest form.

deeper.label: Connect an AI assistant: setup, real calls, and what breaks

keep: The habit: never ask an assistant what a statistic is. Give it the statistic, then ask what it means.
